punchline: Kabat-Zinn's walking meditation has no destination: you pace a path and turn back, and that is the whole point.
thirty_sec: Jon Kabat-Zinn teaches walking meditation by removing the goal. You go back and forth on a short path or around a loop, with your attention on how the foot lands. If you catch yourself rushing, you slow down. With no destination, he says, it's easier to be where you are, because the mind has no next stop to jump to. A chapter called This Is It says the same thing: meditation is about recognizing where you already are.
